request.instructions:
You are writing a plain-language summary of an as-filed Tennessee House bill for an adult reader without legal training.

Use only the bill text supplied in the user message. Treat it as a proposal at introduction, not as proof that it became law or describes current law. Do not use outside knowledge, bill descriptions, later legislative history, or the unstated contents of cited statutes.

Write a neutral summary in prose. Start with what the bill would change. Cover its distinct material provisions, including affected people or organizations, new or changed duties and rights, eligibility rules, amounts and thresholds, deadlines, exceptions, reporting or enforcement requirements, and effective dates when stated. Preserve the bill's conditions and legal distinctions; do not turn a permission into a requirement or a proposal into an enacted rule.

Use familiar words and short, complete sentences. Explain a technical term when the supplied text gives enough context; otherwise retain it rather than guess. Distinguish background or WHEREAS statements from operative provisions, and mention background only when it helps explain the bill. If the bill amends or repeals a cited section without showing that section's contents, describe the textual change and citation without inventing the prior rule or its wider effects.

Keep the summary substantially shorter than the source while retaining the main independent changes. A very short bill may need only one or two sentences; a multi-section bill may need several short paragraphs. Do not add opinions, predicted consequences, a readability score, a confidence rating, headings, bullet points, or a list of citations. Return only the fields required by the supplied output schema.
request.input:
Bill number: HB2256

<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 2332
 By Gardenhire

 HOUSE BILL 2256

 By Sparks

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to public charter schools.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-108(b)(5)(E), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (E) Notwithstanding subdivision (b)(5)(D), a public charter school authorized by

 the commission, and the local board of education of the LEA in which the public charter

 school is located, may, within thirty (30) calendar days of the public charter school's

 authorization, mutually agree in writing that the local board of education will be the

 authorizer and the LEA for the public charter school, and the local board of education

 shall assume the rights and responsibilities of the charter agreement. The charter

 agreement must be filed with the commission in a manner prescribed by the

 commission. This subdivision (b)(5)(E) does not apply to a public charter school that

 has had its charter agreement renewed on appeal by the commission; and

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-110(b)(1), is amended by

deleting "A charter agreement" and substituting "An initial charter agreement".

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-110(c), is amended by

deleting the subsection and substituting:

 (c)

 (1) If a public charter school renewal application is approved by a local

 board of education, then the term of the renewed charter agreement must be for

 ten (10) academic years.

 (2) If a public charter school renewal application is approved by the

 commission, then the term of the renewed charter agreement must be for a term

 of no less than five (5) academic years, but no more than ten (10) academic

 years, as determined by resolution of the commission.

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(g), is amended by

deleting the subsection and substituting:

 (g)

 (1) If a public charter school renewal application is approved by a local

 board of education, then the term of the renewed charter agreement must be for

 ten (10) academic years.

 (2) If a public charter school renewal application is approved by the

 commission, then the term of the renewed charter agreement must be for a term

 of no less than five (5) academic years, but no more than ten (10) academic

 years, as determined by resolution of the commission.

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(f)(3), is amended by

deleting "Notwithstanding subsection (g), the first sentence of § 49-13-110(b), and § 49-13-

110(c), if" and substituting "If".

 SECTION 6. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(l), is amended by deleting

"Notwithstanding subsection (g), the first sentence of § 49-13-110(b), and § 49-13-110(c), if"

and substituting "If".

 SECTION 7. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

summary:
The bill would let a local school board take over as authorizer and local education agency for a commission-authorized public charter school if the board and school mutually agree in writing within 30 calendar days after the school is authorized. The board would assume the charter agreement’s rights and responsibilities, and the agreement would have to be filed with the commission as the commission directs. This option would not apply to a school whose charter agreement was renewed on appeal by the commission.

For charter renewals approved by a local board, the renewed agreement would last 10 academic years. For renewals approved by the commission, it would last between 5 and 10 academic years, as set by commission resolution. The bill makes these term rules in two sections of Tennessee law and changes a reference in another provision from “a charter agreement” to “an initial charter agreement.”

In two provisions, the bill would replace language stating that a condition applies notwithstanding certain other provisions with the word “If.” The bill would take effect upon becoming law.
